1.pericope_label: And I said, Hear, I pray you, O heads of Jacob, and ye princes of the house of Israel; Is it not for you to know judgment? Who hate the good, and love the evil; who pluck off their skin from off them, and their flesh from off their bones; Who also eat the flesh of my people, and flay their skin from off them; and they break their bones, and chop them in pieces, as for the pot, and as flesh within the caldron
debates: Whom the address is delivered to
Whether knowing judgment means understanding it or doing it
Why greater power calls for greater restraint
outliers: Clarke and Calvin both cite an emperor’s answer that a shepherd shears and does not skin
Calvin notes the whole book could have been delivered in half an hour
Ellicott sets an older prophet’s words beside the refused cry
themes: Judges who know faces instead of causes
A flock skinned rather than shorn
Bones broken to reach the marrow

5.pericope_label: Thus saith the Lord concerning the prophets that make my people err, that bite with their teeth, and cry, Peace; and he that putteth not into their mouths, they even prepare war against him. Therefore night shall be unto you, that ye shall not have a vision; and it shall be dark unto you, that ye shall not divine. Then shall the seers be ashamed, and the diviners confounded: yea, they shall all cover their lips; for there is no answer of God
debates: What biting with the teeth means
Whether the night takes away a gift they really had
Whether covering the lips is mourning or silence
outliers: Calvin calls the mourning interpretation of the covered lip frigid
Ellicott notes the word for bite is properly used of serpents
Gill denies these men had any prophetic gift that could be withdrawn
themes: Peace promised to whoever pays for it
A war declared against an unpaid prophet
Night given as the wage of false vision
A mantle cast away by men who had gloried in it

8.pericope_label: But truly I am full of power by the spirit of the Lord, and of judgment, and of might, to declare unto Jacob his transgression, and to Israel his sin. Hear this, I pray you, ye heads of the house of Jacob, and princes of the house of Israel, that abhor judgment, and pervert all equity
debates: Whether the claim to power is boasting
What the three gifts named amount to
Why the Spirit is named before the charge is laid
outliers: Calvin says the name of God works as a hidden chain on men who would otherwise rage
Henry asks what the chaff is to the wheat, or painted fire to real fire
Calvin draws from the verse a lesson for teachers outnumbered by false ones
themes: A man who dares not soften what he was given to say
Discernment between the precious and the vile
A crowd appealing to its own size as a shield
A boast confirmed in the next breath

10.pericope_label: They build up Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity. The heads thereof judge for reward, and the priests thereof teach for hire, and the prophets thereof divine for money: yet will they lean upon the Lord, and say, Is not the Lord among us? none evil can come upon us. Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of the forest
debates: Whether building with blood means murder or plunder
Whether every judge who takes payment is condemned
How and when the sentence on the city was fulfilled
outliers: Clarke applies the verse to fortunes made from the slave trade
Ellicott records that this prophecy was cited a century later to save another prophet’s life
Gill excepts the reigning king from the charge and dates the prophecy early in his reign
themes: Houses whose timbers are bones and whose mortar is blood
Three offices all carried on by bribes
A temple leaned on by men who had polluted it
A plough drawn over the walls of a city
